indicators.label: Immigrants arriving per year
indicators.definition: People who established their usual residence in the country during the year, of any citizenship (including returning nationals).

breaks.note: From 2008 Spain's figures come from INE's Migration Statistics; earlier years are derived from residential-change records (EVR) and are not fully comparable.

indicators.label: Immigrants arriving per 1,000 residents
indicators.definition: Annual immigration flow divided by the population on 1 January, times 1,000 (our calculation from two Eurostat tables).

breaks.note: From 2008 Spain's figures come from INE's Migration Statistics; earlier years are derived from residential-change records (EVR) and are not fully comparable.

indicators.label: People living in the country who were born abroad
indicators.definition: Resident population on 1 January born outside the reporting country, regardless of current citizenship. Includes Spanish citizens born abroad.
indicators.notes: Spain's population register (Padrón) also records many migrants without legal residence, because registering gives access to healthcare and schooling, so coverage of irregular migrants is better than in most countries.

indicators.label: Share of the population born abroad
indicators.definition: Foreign-born residents as a percentage of the total resident population on 1 January (our calculation).
indicators.notes: Spain's population register (Padrón) also records many migrants without legal residence.

indicators.label: Net migration per 1,000 residents
indicators.definition: Arrivals minus departures (plus statistical adjustment) per 1,000 average population. Negative values mean more people left than arrived.

indicators.label: Intentional homicide recorded by police
indicators.definition: Unlawful death inflicted on a person with the intent to cause death or serious injury.

source.upstream: Spanish Ministry of the Interior (police-recorded offences)

indicators.notes: Police-recorded offences reflect both crime and how often victims report it and police record it. Legal definitions differ between countries, so Eurostat advises against direct cross-country comparison of levels.

indicators.label: Serious assault recorded by police
indicators.definition: Intentional or reckless application of force causing serious bodily injury.

indicators.label: Sexual violence recorded by police
indicators.definition: Offences of rape (ICCS 03011) and sexual assault (ICCS 03012) recorded by police. Counts offences known to police, not victims, arrests, prosecutions or convictions.

breaks.note: Spain's Criminal Code reform (LO 1/2015) raised the age of sexual consent to 16 and abolished minor offences ('faltas').

Organic Law 10/2022 ('only yes means yes', in force October 2022) removed the legal distinction between sexual 'abuse' and sexual 'aggression': all non-consensual sexual acts became sexual aggression.

indicators.label: Intentional homicide (long series)
indicators.definition: Intentional homicides per 100,000 people, compiled by UNODC from national criminal justice and public-health sources.
indicators.notes: The only crime measure available as a consistent series for Spain back to the early 2000s.

indicators.label: Size of the economy (real GDP)
indicators.definition: Gross domestic product in chain-linked volumes (2010 euros), removing the effect of inflation.
indicators.notes: GDP grows mechanically when the population grows; GDP per person is a better guide to average living standards.

indicators.label: Real GDP per person
indicators.definition: Real GDP divided by population (chain-linked volumes, 2010 euros).

indicators.label: People in work
indicators.definition: Total employment (domestic concept, national accounts), in millions of people.

indicators.label: Unemployment rate
indicators.definition: Unemployed people aged 15–74 as a percentage of the labour force (Labour Force Survey, ILO definition).

indicators.label: House prices after inflation
indicators.definition: Nominal house price index deflated by the consumer price index.

indicators.label: House prices
indicators.definition: Nominal residential property price index.

indicators.label: Rents
indicators.definition: Rent component of the consumer price index.
indicators.notes: In Spain this index tracks rents paid on all existing contracts, so it rises far more slowly than asking rents for new contracts (e.g. listing portals or INE's experimental rental index).

indicators.label: Rents after inflation
indicators.definition: Rent index divided by the overall consumer price index (HICP), both 2015 = 100 (our calculation). Above 100 means rents rose faster than prices in general since 2015.
indicators.notes: In Spain this index tracks rents on all existing contracts, so it understates the rise in rents for new tenants.

indicators.label: House prices relative to incomes
indicators.definition: Nominal house prices divided by nominal disposable income per person. Higher means housing is less affordable.

indicators.label: House prices relative to rents
indicators.definition: Nominal house prices divided by the rent index.

indicators.label: Average annual wage after inflation
indicators.definition: Average annual wages per full-time-equivalent employee, at constant prices (latest-year euros).

indicators.label: Household income after inflation, per person
indicators.definition: Real adjusted gross disposable income of households per person: income after taxes and benefits, including the value of public services such as health and education, adjusted for inflation.

indicators.label: Typical (median) income after inflation
indicators.definition: Median equivalised net income from the EU-SILC survey, deflated by the HICP (our calculation). Survey year shown; incomes refer to the previous calendar year.

indicators.label: Income inequality (Gini coefficient)
indicators.unit: 0 = everyone equal, 100 = one person has everything
indicators.definition: Gini coefficient of equivalised disposable income (EU-SILC). Higher means more unequal. Survey year shown; incomes refer to the previous calendar year.

breaks.note: Eurostat flags a break in Spain's series this year: figures before and after are not fully comparable.

indicators.label: Material living standards vs EU average
indicators.definition: Actual individual consumption per person in purchasing power standards, relative to the EU-27 average (= 100). Accounts for price differences between countries.
